newsitem.title: INDIA: India contracts 125,000T sunflower oil imports.
newsitem.headline: India contracts 125,000T sunflower oil imports.

text.p: India has so far contracted for imports of nearly 125,000 tonnes of sunflower oil for January, February and March shipments, industry officials said on Friday.

"Importers have contracted for nearly 125,000 tonnes of sunflower oil for shipments during the next three months," Navin Bhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange told Reuters by telephone.
Traders said Indian traders were importing sunflower oil at around $575-600 per tonne CIF.
"Importers are getting a premium on sunflower oil when they sell it in the local markets," Shah said.
Traders said Indian importers were selling the imported sunflower oil at around 1,000 rupees more a tonne than the imported price.
"But palm olein prices are stagnant. Buyers sell it at a much less premium than sunflower. Therefore, they prefer sunflower," Shah said.

Traders said palm olein was currently imported at around $575 per tonne FOB. "At what (prices) we are getting sunflower oil at landed cost in Bombay, we are getting palm olein at the same price FOB at Malaysian ports," Shah said.
